value: A module is a fundamental algebraic structure that generalizes the concepts of a vector space and an abelian group. It consists of an additive abelian group equipped with a scalar multiplication operation by elements of a ring, rather than a field (as in vector spaces) or the integers (as in abelian groups), satisfying specific axioms of distributivity and associativity. Modules are central to various fields of mathematics, including commutative and homological algebra, algebraic geometry, algebraic topology, and notably representation theory, where group representations can be viewed as modules over a group ring. While sharing many properties with vector spaces, modules can be more complex; for instance, not all modules have a basis, and their rank is not always unique. The rich theory also classifies modules into diverse types such as free, projective, injective, and simple modules, reflecting their varied structural characteristics.
